messages.glossary.note: Common pattern-making terms, in French and English. Translations not validated by a pattern maker: those marked "to be validated" are the least certain.
messages.glossary.t.armhole.def: Opening of the garment where the sleeve is set.
messages.glossary.t.bias.def: Direction at 45 degrees to the fabric thread, where it stretches most.
messages.glossary.t.block.def: Plain starting pattern that is transformed to obtain a design.
messages.glossary.t.buttonhole.def: Reinforced slit through which a button passes.
messages.glossary.t.calibration_square.def: 100 mm square printed to check the printer scale.
messages.glossary.t.center_back.def: Vertical axis in the middle of the back of the garment.
messages.glossary.t.center_front.def: Vertical axis in the middle of the front of the garment.
messages.glossary.t.cutting_line.def: Outline of the piece to cut, seam allowances included.
messages.glossary.t.dart.def: Pointed sewn fold that shapes the fabric: an apex and two legs.
messages.glossary.t.ease.def: Room added to the body measurements so that the garment can be worn.
messages.glossary.t.fold.def: Piece edge placed on the fold of the fabric: the piece is cut in one go.
messages.glossary.t.gathers.def: Small close folds made by pulling a thread, to shorten a length of fabric.
messages.glossary.t.grading.def: Derivation of a pattern into several sizes.
messages.glossary.t.grainline.def: Direction of the fabric thread, parallel to the selvedge, shown as an arrow on the piece.
messages.glossary.t.hem.def: Edge folded and sewn to finish the bottom of a piece.
messages.glossary.t.interfacing.def: Stiffener fused or sewn to the wrong side of a piece to support it.
messages.glossary.t.lining.def: Fabric that covers the inside of a garment or a bag.
messages.glossary.t.nap.def: Direction of the pile or print: all pieces are cut the same way.
messages.glossary.t.neckline.def: Outline of the garment opening around the neck.
messages.glossary.t.nesting.def: Layout of pieces or stacked sizes on a single sheet.
messages.glossary.t.notch.def: Small mark on the cut edge to match two pieces when sewing.
messages.glossary.t.pattern.def: The set of pieces to cut to make a garment or an object.
messages.glossary.t.pattern_piece.def: One shape to cut from the material, with its grainline, notches and allowances.
messages.glossary.t.pleat.def: Excess fabric folded and held; flat or hollow depending on the folding direction.
messages.glossary.t.seam_allowance.def: Strip of fabric between the sewing line and the cutting line.
messages.glossary.t.selvedge.def: Finished edge of the fabric, along the warp.
messages.glossary.t.sewing_line.def: Outline along which the pieces are joined.
messages.glossary.t.sheet.def: Working space of the software: it is not a printed page.
messages.glossary.t.size_range.def: Ordered list of the sizes of a project, with a base size.
messages.glossary.t.skiving.def: Thinning of leather in an area, before folding or gluing.
messages.glossary.t.stitch_holes.def: Evenly spaced holes for hand sewing (leatherwork).
messages.glossary.t.topstitch.def: Visible stitching on the right side, parallel to an edge.
messages.glossary.title: Glossary

messages.guide.step.1.body: A sheet is a workspace, not a page. Rename it in the sheets panel, or create one per piece. Measurements are in millimetres.
messages.guide.step.1.title: Prepare the sheet
messages.guide.step.2.body: Pick the Segment tool: click the start, then type the length and the angle (Tab moves between fields), Enter confirms. Shift locks the angle in 15° steps.
messages.guide.step.2.title: Draw a first segment
messages.guide.step.3.body: Chain segments, curves and arcs to close the piece outline. Give each outline path the Sewing role: roles are shown by a line style and a name, never by colour alone.
messages.guide.step.3.title: Close the outline
messages.guide.step.4.body: Pick the Extract a piece tool and click inside the closed area. The piece card gives its area and perimeter, measured on the drawing.
messages.guide.step.4.title: Extract the piece
messages.guide.step.5.body: Draw the grainline with the Grainline tool (start, then end), parallel to the fabric selvedge. A piece without a grainline stays valid, but a warning flags it.
messages.guide.step.5.title: Set the grainline
messages.guide.step.6.body: Pick the Notch tool, click the path that carries it and enter the distance from the path start. Notches are assembly marks.
messages.guide.step.6.title: Add notches
messages.guide.step.7.body: In the piece card, declare the seam allowances (default value, per-edge value, hem). The cut outline is computed; the sewing drawing is never modified.
messages.guide.step.7.title: Seam allowances
messages.guide.step.8.body: Export a 1:1 PDF, print the calibration page and measure the 100 mm square before cutting. A complete example is under Help, Example projects.
messages.guide.step.8.title: Export and check

messages.inspector.imposed.formula.hint: Expression on the variables (for example bust / 4 + 12). The length follows the formula when a variable changes.
messages.inspector.imposed.note: Developed length held to 1e-6 mm: a handle or an end point adjusts, also when its parents move. Impossible = the change is refused.
messages.inspector.imposed.off.hover: Removes the imposed length; the current geometry is kept.
messages.inspector.imposed.offset.hint: A number, or a formula on the variables (for example ease * 2): the offset then follows the variable.

messages.inspector.notch.anchor.note.carried: The point is projected onto the source path; the distance obtained from the start of that path is carried onto the notch's path. Refused if it exceeds the length of the notch's path. Source and point are on the same sheet.
messages.inspector.notch.anchor.note.fixed: Fixed distance: the notch stays at the typed distance from the start of the path. Pick another mode to tie it to a point or a proportion.
messages.inspector.notch.anchor.note.midpoint: The notch sits at the middle of the path, by developed length for a curve. It follows the path when its length changes.
messages.inspector.notch.anchor.note.point: The notch sits at the foot of the perpendicular dropped from this point onto the path (not necessarily on the point itself). It follows the point when it moves; if the point is deleted, the notch is removed.
messages.inspector.notch.anchor.note.ratio: The notch sits at this proportion of the path length, from its start (0 % = start, 100 % = end). It follows the path when its length changes.
messages.inspector.notch.corner.failed: Vertex not identifiable, falling back to the path normal: {reason}
messages.inspector.notch.corner.note: The notch is placed at a vertex of the seam (start or end of its path) and oriented along the bisector of the angle of the piece outline; it follows the vertex when it moves. The side chooses the outside or the inside of the piece. Not compatible with "On the cutting line" (postponed).
messages.inspector.notch.note: The side is read in the start -> end direction of the path. The notch follows its path when it is moved or transformed.
messages.inspector.notch.on_cut: On the cutting line (projected from the seam)
messages.inspector.notch.on_cut.note: The notch is projected perpendicular to the seam, towards the outside of the piece, onto the computed cutting contour: its position follows the margin. The side has no effect; the depth is counted from the cutting contour towards the seam.
messages.inspector.notch.proportional.anchored: Unavailable: the notch is anchored, it already follows its edge.
messages.inspector.notch.proportional.note: In each size the notch keeps the same fraction of its path length instead of a fixed distance. The base size does not change.
